claims.statement: The literal fixed-selector deletion-plus-two-for-one weighted network has an integral flow saturating all upper supply on the deterministic first five stored eligible p=7 rows at each of orders 16, 17, and 18, 15 rows total. Their complete original-leaf sums are negative.
claims.scope: Only those 15 stored-order rows from the pinned order-16 and corrected-scope order-17/18 census results; original strict selector and all original leaf tags; no regenerated census or universal inference.
claims.reason: retained: route and both critics agree; adjudicator checked guards, selected terms, S=upper-lower, saturation totals, and zero deficits in the packaged exact rows. Critics replayed the network and CU audited arc legality and capacities. The remaining 4,976 reported eligible p=7 rows were not flow-tested.

claims.statement: CB(8,92) at p=492 and CB(8,93) at p=498 are eligible strict lower-region ordinary-tree rows, all original leaves are favorable, and each exact complete selected sum S is negative.
claims.scope: Exactly the two CB(8,m) trees and ranks, with arm leaf multiplicity one and branch leaf multiplicity 8m; exact bounded polynomial computation only.
claims.reason: retained: both rows have terminal-aware first descent, all original arm and branch tags, strict selector checks and negative multiplicity-weighted complete sums. The supplied cut-envelope lower bounds are negative and prove no deficient cut.

claims.statement: For each independent upper set containing h and v in the two stated CB rows, the complete legal exact two-neighbor switch targets are arm support s and precisely those chokes c_i whose branch has one occupied support; aggregate arc counts are exact.
claims.scope: Only h,v-containing upper sets in CB(8,92),p=492 and CB(8,93),p=498; no classification for other source sets and no full-flow claim.
claims.reason: retained: direct neighborhood exhaustion verifies s has occupied neighbors h,v; c_i has h plus its occupied supports; absent supports and leaves have at most one. Both critics agree and branch-polynomial arc counts are preserved in the packaged evidence.

claims.statement: In each stated CB row, every h,v-containing upper source with a branch having one occupied support and at least four occupied leaves among its other seven pairs can route one unit by its first qualifying choke switch within lower node capacities; the exact routed and unrouted supplies are recorded.
claims.scope: Only the specified qualifying source subfamily of CB(8,92),p=492 and CB(8,93),p=498; full upper-supply saturation is unproved.
claims.reason: retained: the move deletes exactly h and the occupied support, then inserts its choke. A destination with ell>=4 branch leaves has at most 8-ell preimages and capacity at least ell. The coefficient formula counts the routed family exactly; both critics verified the proof and positive unrouted supply remains.

claims.statement: Among 633 canonical hub-tree branch-multiset recipes of order at most 18, all 138 eligible rank rows have nonpositive complete selected sums and saturated integral flow under all deletion and literal two-for-one arcs.
claims.scope: Only 2..5 sorted branches of types P1..P4 or C2..C4, order <=18, and all ranks satisfying both target guards within that family; same-implementation replay, not a universal result.
claims.reason: retained: both critics reproduce the 633/138 counts, flow saturation and S range -9828..-224; the adjudicator checked the exact P2,C3,C4 representative including all eight leaf tags and S=-275=259-534. The full sweep depends on the source generator and its replays.

claims.statement: For n=2p+2+d (d>=1), k=p-1, H_v=T-{v,s_v}, W_v=N_T(s_v)\{v}, an ordering of W_v whose every union N_H[w_i] with earlier mark vertices has size at least d+3 makes the v summand nonpositive. If every v in the fixed F(T,p) has such an ordering, S(T,p)<=0. The source cover-number lower bound is false.
claims.scope: Exact sufficient structural subclass of the primary ordinary-tree setting; no implication from eligibility or favorability to the size condition. Cover bound rejected even for K2.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: first-mark partition and independent-set incidence prove the subclass. K2 with full vertex cover at r=1 has claimed L=-1 but actual Delta_1=-2; the positive a=r+1 cover contribution was replaced by an upper bound. Both critics found this defect.

claims.reason: retained: a symmetric chain on the m-1 leaves other than each tag contains ranks p and p-1; its predecessor is a one-leaf deletion, retains a witness since p-1>=1, and is injective within and across tag fibers.

claims.statement: At n=2p+3, k=p-1, first-mark residuals satisfy |J_i|=2k+3-deg_H(w_i)-i because marks are pairwise nonadjacent. Thus size 2k+2 can arise at (i,deg)=(1,0), size 2k+1 at (1,1) or (2,0), and size 2k at (1,2),(2,1), or (3,0). Residuals of order <=2k-1 have i_k<=i_(k-1); for k edges plus one isolate the difference is 2^(k-2)(4-binomial(k,2)).
claims.scope: Odd parent shell structural and exact graph-subclass results only; no full selected-sum sign or guarded matching realization.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the first-mark identity, small-residual shadow bound, and matching coefficient formula survive. The source and F-critic boundary inventories omit isolated marks. The U-critic 23-vertex eligible example has an isolated second mark and a size-2k+1 residual despite ordering a nonisolated mark first; its full S=-44250.

claims.statement: At p=9, explicit T4 and its one-leaf graft at root 0 both have alpha=14, x=7, and 27<29. All 13 old original leaves remain strictly favorable and new leaf 19 is favorable. Their complete selected sums are -10089 and -17280.

claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T with p>=3, |V(T)|=2p+2 and x(T)+2<=p, each original leaf v has Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v])<=0; hence the sum over the fixed strict favorable selector is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Exact first parent-order shell; no alpha-region premise is needed for the pointwise assertion. Informal proof depends on the marked-cover shell lemma, registered exact first-wide graph classification and binomial-difference Catalan floor.
claims.reason: retained: the cover-three all-earlier-ranks contradiction forces tau(T)>=4; pendant exchange gives tau(H_v)>=3 and a nonisolated mark, so the marked-cover lemma applies at k=p-1. Both critics checked the boundaries. No larger-order conclusion.

claims.statement: For a finite simple graph G with |V(G)|=2k+2, k>=2, tau(G)>=3, and marks W containing a nonisolated vertex, the number q_(k+1) of independent sets meeting W is at most q_k.
claims.scope: Exact graph order, cover and mark hypotheses; informal deduction using only the registered first-wide classification at order 2(k-1)+2=2k.
claims.reason: retained: split marked sets at a nonisolated mark; smaller residuals satisfy incidence shadow bounds, while exact-order residuals retain at least two edges by tau>=3 and satisfy the first-wide classification. The second split term uses the proved order-at-most-2k+1 auxiliary bound.

claims.statement: An unweighted one-step subset-shadow statement, including the colored-shadow result described by C3-U4, does not by itself establish fixed-selector weighted deletion-plus-two-for-one cut inequalities.
claims.scope: Direct-application check only; switch outputs insert an absent vertex and the network has selector-dependent capacities. The exact external bibliographic theorem and any refined bridge are outside the verified claim.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: both critics identified the subset-versus-switch and unweighted-versus-weighted mismatches; neither independently audited the precise primary-paper hypotheses, so only direct non-implication survives.

claims.statement: For a finite bipartite transport relation with nonnegative upper supplies u, lower capacities c and uncapacitated relation arcs, full supply saturation holds iff u(X)<=c(N(X)) for every upper subset X; g(X)=c(N(X))-u(X) is submodular and its minimizers are closed under union and intersection.
claims.scope: General finite transport with the stated arc capacities; this criterion does not show tree-derived cuts pass, and a failed cut alone does not refute the scalar aggregate.
claims.reason: retained: max-flow/min-cut yields the all-subset criterion, weighted neighborhood coverage is submodular, and subtraction of modular supply preserves it. Both critics checked the finite-network argument.

claims.statement: For a finite group action preserving a finite bipartite transport relation, supplies and capacities, quotienting by vertex orbits preserves saturating-flow feasibility exactly; it applies to each fixed eligible tree under selector-preserving automorphisms.
claims.scope: Fixed finite invariant instances, retaining actual orbit-pair adjacency; no uniform tree cut inequality or guaranteed small quotient.
claims.reason: retained: nonempty orbit-pair relations are biregular, so quotient flow spreads uniformly to literal edges; literal flow aggregates back. Integral max-flow converts lifted fractional feasibility to integral feasibility for integer capacities.

claims.statement: For an eligible ordinary tree T,p with fixed F, let k=p-1, Q be the total number of selected-leaf-tagged independent k-sets in H_v meeting W_v, E their total actual addable-vertex count, and E_x=(x+1)i_(x+1)(T)/i_x(T). If E<=E_x Q, then S(T,p)<=0, strictly if Q>0.
claims.scope: Conditional theorem at the exact contract selector and rank guards; the transfer premise E<=E_x Q is not established for all eligible trees.
claims.reason: retained: first descent gives E_x<x+1<=k; marked bipartite extension counting gives kS=(2a+1-3p)Q-sum(D_v+C_v), with sum D_v=2(a-p)Q-E and C_v>=0. The premise supplies the missing budget; Q=0 is handled separately.

limitations: The universal ordinary-tree lower-region complete selected aggregate is neither proved nor refuted by the three adjudicator portfolios.
The universal expanded two-for-one weighted Hall assertion has no all-cut proof or deficient expanded-relation cut; it is stronger than the scalar target.
The corrected graft computation covers two trees at p=9; the original reported complete sums omitted an original selected leaf.
The universal per-selected-leaf marked-down injectivity premise is refuted on eligible T22, although its conditional implication remains valid.
The first-shell proof is informal and the rank-through-seven composition depends on registered forest maxima and complete residual censuses that were not rerun here.
Finite flow and family sweeps retain their stored-row, generation-boundary and replay dependencies; no new census, full flow replay, Lean build or external theorem audit was performed.
